rv.q: These episodes are meaningful and occasionally humorous, but they tend to interfere with the natural rhythm of the drama.
Serdar Biliş reaches back over two millennia to adapt Euripides’ Iphigenia in Aulis and makes it speak, pointedly, uncomfortably, insistently to us, right here, right now.
But rather than disrupting flow, these moments effectively imbue the play’s classical exchanges with a modern sense of jeopardy and desperation.
This Iphigenia compellingly draws out contemporary parallels, including witness from the cast, yet leaves Euripides intact.

cn.t: An earnest but underpowered production that awkwardly blends Euripides' tragedy with contemporary testimonials about violence. Strong performances can't overcome the ill-conceived staging, though timely themes resonate.
